channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description: Mahomes ran the ball seven times for 23 yards and one touchdown last week before practicing in full this week. Both factors are encouraging. The Chiefs’ star quarterback warrants QB1 treatment against the Colts in Week 2.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description: Rice earned only two targets in Week 1, yet still technically warrants WR2 treatment based on his theoretical role in the offense, along with his past WR1 performances. The Chiefs notably faced the Broncos’ top-tier defense last week and will get a far softer matchup against the Colts in Week 2.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
item.description: Horton’s return boosts QB Drew Lock’s passing outlook, though Horton is not worth starting in 12-team FLEX spots, operating in the Seahawks WR4 role.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chiefs DT Chris Jones (calf) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane (shoulder) is also questionable to play this week, though Chiefs coach Andy Reid said earlier this week “there’s a pretty good chance” Delane will suit up in Week 1. Jones remained limited all week. Delane logged two full sessions before downgrading to limited on Friday, which could indicate he suffered a setback. We will find out soon enough.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 2 against the Colts.
item.description: Backup OT Kahlil Benson will start in Simmons’ stead. He did so last week and avoided major mistakes. The Chiefs also ruled out CB Chamarri Conner (knee).-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle/hip) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Cardinals.
item.description: Emmanwori picked up a hip injury mid-week. Hopefully, he is good to go by Sunday. The Seahawks ruled out fellow starting S Ty Okada (hamstring) for this one, but the Seahawks D/ST remains formidable overall.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) is questionable for Week 2 against the Raiders.
item.description: McConkey managed a limited session Friday and eventually drew the questionable tag as he attempts to play through a rib injury suffered in Week 1. Considering his value to this team, we would expect him to do what he can to play. That said, fantasy managers find themselves in a pickle with the Chargers not playing until the afternoon portion of games, meaning alternate plans should be in the works over the weekend. McConkey is a locked-in WR2 with WR1 upside, if active.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Commanders WR Jaylin Lane (groin) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cowboys.
item.description: Lane caught 1-of-1 targets for four yards last week. He is not on the fantasy radar for 12-team managed leagues, although it is nice to know that his groin is feeling better. Commanders rookie WR Antonio Williams has seemingly leapfrogged Lane after one game.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Commanders RB Kaytron Allen (knee/ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Cowboys.
item.description: Allen practiced in full all week, so there are no concerns about his current status. Last week, starting RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt fumbled late in the game and was yanked for the final eight plays. Last Man Standig’s Ben Standig notes, Allen “handled the final three handoffs, and Rachaad White was a potential safety valve” for the Commanders’ two-point attempt. Allen is worth stashing on benches in 12-team leagues.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 2 against the Bengals.
item.description: Collins was added to the injury report on Thursday and will miss Week 2 with yet another soft tissue injury. Considering his lengthy history of hamstring issues, we would not be surprised if this turned into a multi-game absence for the talented alpha. Expect Kayshon Boutte to see an uptick in routes, while it is likely Xavier Hutchinson kicks to the perimeter to make room for Jaylin Noel in the slot. Collins’ absence benefits veteran tight end Dalton Schultz the most, whom enters the TE1 ranks in a matchup made in heaven against the inside-funnel Bengals.-Mark Garcia
